---
title: "Gallery"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

# One horizontal slider per section. Images live in pkgdown/assets/gallery/,
# which pkgdown copies to the site root; pkgdown/extra.js wires the arrows.
slider <- function(label, items) {
  href <- if ("href" %in% names(items)) items$href else items$file
  slides <- Map(
    function(file, alt, href) {
      htmltools::tags$a(
        href = href,
        htmltools::tags$img(src = file, alt = alt, loading = "lazy")
      )
    },
    items$file,
    items$alt,
    href
  )
  htmltools::div(
    class = "gallery-slider",
    htmltools::tags$button(
      type = "button",
      class = "gallery-prev",
      `aria-label` = "Previous chart",
      htmltools::HTML("&larr;")
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      class = "gallery-track",
      tabindex = "0",
      role = "region",
      `aria-label` = label,
      slides
    ),
    htmltools::tags$button(
      type = "button",
      class = "gallery-next",
      `aria-label` = "Next chart",
      htmltools::HTML("&rarr;")
    )
  )
}

viz <- function(file) paste0("../gallery/ekio-viz/", file, ".png")
insights <- function(file) paste0("../gallery/insights/", file, ".png")
post <- function(slug) paste0("https://ekio.io/insights/posts/", slug, "/")
```

Charts built with `ekioplot` for EKIO's data visualization work. Click a chart
to open it at full size.

## EKIO-viz

[EKIO-viz](https://github.com/viniciusoike/ekio-viz) collects standalone
charts on the Brazilian economy, cities, and society. Each chart has its R
script in the repository.

### Real estate

```{r}
slider("Real estate charts from EKIO-viz", tibble::tribble(
  ~file, ~alt,
  viz("01-house-vs-rent"), "Two panels of line charts. In Brazil the house price index (IGMI-R) reaches about 235 since Dec/2018 while the rent index (IVAR) reaches about 140; the lower panel repeats the comparison for four capitals.",
  viz("02-prices-inflation"), "Line chart showing the IVG-R house price index rising to nearly 800 since March 2001, above construction costs (INCC) near 650 and consumer inflation (IPCA) near 450.",
  viz("03-indices-diverging"), "Two panels. The upper line chart chains the three Brazilian house price indices from Jan/2014, with IGMI-R pulling away after 2021 while FipeZap and the IVG-R stay close to 150. The lower panel shows the 12-month change of each index.",
  viz("09-cities-beat-inflation"), "Eight waffle grids, one per year from 2018 to 2025, with one tile per Brazilian city coloured by whether rents, sale prices, both or neither rose faster than inflation. From 2022 on most tiles turn blue as both series beat inflation."
))
```

### Economy

```{r}
slider("Economy charts from EKIO-viz", tibble::tribble(
  ~file, ~alt,
  viz("04-world-wealth"), "Stacked area chart of regional shares of world GDP from 1950 to 2022, with selected countries in stronger shades. China rises from 5.2 to 20.7 percent while the United States falls from 27.5 to 14.9 percent.",
  viz("12-focus-gdp"), "Dodged bar chart comparing the median January Focus forecast for Brazil's GDP growth from 2017 to 2026 with realized growth through 2025. The market expected 2.3 percent in 2020, when GDP fell 3.3 percent.",
  viz("21-selic-real-rate"), "Two stacked line charts from 1999 to 2026. The top panel shows the Selic target, in two digits in 74 percent of months. The bottom panel shows the 12-month real interest rate, negative only in 2020-22.",
  viz("26-misery-index"), "Stacked area chart of Brazil's misery index, the sum of unemployment and 12-month inflation, from 2012 to 2026. It peaked at 23.0 percent in September 2021 and stood at 9.9 percent in September 2026.",
  viz("37-debt-gdp-headlines"), "Line chart of Brazil's gross government debt from 2014 to 2026, with thin lines for each January's Focus forecast, nearly all above the realized path, and circles marking news headlines on the fiscal outlook.",
  viz("22-economy-scorecard"), "Colour-coded table comparing eight presidential terms, from FHC I to Lula III, at month 42 of each term on GDP growth, unemployment, employment, labour income, inflation, and the real Ibovespa.",
  viz("35-working-age-waves"), "Line chart of the share of the population aged 15 to 64 from 1960 to 2100. Brazil peaks at 69.7 percent in 2017 and then falls faster than other developing countries."
))
```

### Cities and mobility

```{r}
slider("Cities and mobility charts from EKIO-viz", tibble::tribble(
  ~file, ~alt,
  viz("06-inequality-cities"), "Six circular maps of Brazilian cities where census tracts are coloured by within-city household-head income decile, with water in blue and parks in green.",
  viz("28-income-sao-paulo-deciles"), "Two maps of São Paulo comparing 2010 and 2022, with census tracts coloured from purple to orange by household-head income decile.",
  viz("07-long-commutes"), "Horizontal bar chart ranking 20 Brazilian municipalities by the share of workers whose commute takes more than one hour. Francisco Morato leads at 47.9 percent; São Paulo, the only capital, is at 29.2 percent.",
  viz("11-commute-rio-map"), "Map of average commute time by weighting area across the Rio de Janeiro metropolitan region.",
  viz("14-commute-mode-floripa"), "Two-panel choropleth of the Florianópolis metro region coloured by the share of workers who commute by car, taxi or ride-hailing, 45 percent across the metro, with a zoom on the capital.",
  viz("40-car-share-poa"), "Two-panel map of the share of workers who commute by car in the Porto Alegre metro region and a zoom on the capital. Estimates range from 19 to 85 percent.",
  viz("36-traffic-deaths"), "Line chart of annual traffic deaths in Brazil from 1996 to 2024. Deaths peak at 45.9 thousand in 2012, fall to 32.8 thousand in 2019, and rise 16 percent to 38.1 thousand in 2024."
))
```

### Society and politics

```{r}
slider("Society and politics charts from EKIO-viz", tibble::tribble(
  ~file, ~alt,
  viz("05-solo-living"), "Line chart of the share of one-person households in Brazil and four states, all rising between 2012 and 2023; Rio de Janeiro reaches 20.8 percent.",
  viz("25-solo-living-rio-age"), "Dodged bar chart of the share of Rio de Janeiro residents who live alone in 2022, by age group and sex. Men lead up to age 54; beyond 65 the share for women climbs to 31 percent at 75 to 84.",
  viz("17-driver-licenses-age"), "Dumbbell chart of the share of Brazilians holding a driver's licence in 2022, by age band and sex. Only 18 percent of 18 to 21 year olds hold one, and men lead women in every band.",
  viz("38-hot-days-capitals"), "Heatmap of the 27 Brazilian state capitals by year, from 2001 to 2024, coloured by the number of days at 35 °C or more. Cuiabá peaks at 216 days in 2024.",
  viz("19-congresso-2027"), "Two hemicycles of the Congress that takes office in 2027, one dot per seat, ordered from left to right by ideology, with bars showing seats against majority thresholds.",
  viz("18-election-sp-2022"), "Map of São Paulo's districts split into Voronoi cells, one per polling place, sized by valid votes and coloured by Lula's share in the 2022 presidential runoff."
))
```

## EKIO Insights

[EKIO Insights](https://ekio.io/insights/) publishes short analyses, in
Portuguese, on real estate, the economy, and demographics. Click a chart to
read its post.

```{r}
slider("Charts from EKIO Insights posts", tibble::tribble(
  ~file, ~href, ~alt,
  insights("juros-renda"), post("2023-08-juros-financiamento"), "Line chart of the minimum income needed to finance a home worth R$450 thousand in January 2018, holding the price fixed and updating it by a house price index. After 2020 price gains push the required income above R$18 thousand.",
  insights("affordability-sp"), post("2024-03-affordability-sp"), "Map of the price-to-income ratio by origin-destination zone in São Paulo, 2021, measured in years of household income. Values peak in Jardins and Alto de Pinheiros; zones without data are grey.",
  insights("aluguel-venda"), post("2024-02-aluguel-venda-imoveis"), "Scatter plot of monthly changes in rent and sale prices split at the October 2020 structural break. The positive relationship before the break disappears after it.",
  insights("recessoes"), post("2024-03-recessoes-brasil"), "Line chart of GDP during six Brazilian recessions, indexed to the quarter before each one began. The Covid recession has the deepest drop; the 2014-2016 recession lasts longest.",
  insights("inflacao-historica"), post("2026-01-inflacao-brasil"), "Monthly IPCA inflation from 1980 to November 2025, shaded by presidential term and annotated with economic plans. Inflation is very high until the Plano Real and much lower after 1994.",
  insights("ips-componentes"), post("2024-09-ips-municipios"), "Horizontal bar chart of the average municipal score on each component of the Social Progress Index. Housing scores highest at 86.9 and individual rights lowest at 28.5.",
  insights("metro-crescimento"), post("2025-06-censo-metro-regions"), "Horizontal bar chart of average population growth from 2010 to 2022 by municipality size. Cities of 100 to 500 thousand lead with 14.3 percent; cities above one million grew 1.1 percent.",
  insights("geracoes"), post("2025-02-generations-brazil"), "Column chart of each age's share of Brazil's population in the 2022 Census, coloured by generation. Gen Z and Millennials make up almost half the population.",
  insights("dependencia-mapa"), post("2025-07-demografia-brasil"), "Bivariate map of youth and old-age dependency ratios by Brazilian state in 2022. Northern states have higher youth dependency; Rio Grande do Sul and Rio de Janeiro have higher old-age dependency.",
  insights("piramides"), post("2025-07-demografia-brasil"), "Population pyramids for Amazonas, Piauí, Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina in 2022. Amazonas has the widest base, and Rio Grande do Sul has the most people in older age groups."
))
```
